_meta.description: The SIMPLE structure profile, and the default one (openspec/changes/simple-structure-profile). `menu-layout.json` is the FULL profile and is untouched: an administrator brings it back with the setting `menu_structure`. Both profiles are built from the same manifest and the same fragments, so nothing is deleted and every page stays routable; this file only decides what the navigation offers first. THE STANDARD KEYS (`removals`, `settingsSection`) go to the library's buildManifest exactly as the full file's do. `relocations` is absent: the simple menu is flat and moves nothing. (Before nextcloud-vue 2.84.0 the relocation step also dropped every caption; since #1608 it keeps them.) THE PROFILE KEYS `menu`, `pages`, `nav` and `tours` are read by src/utils/structureProfile.js. `tours` is the contact centre tour: the sales tour points at Contacts, Products, Leads and Contracts, which this menu lacks, so holdUnreachableTours holds it back and without a tour of its own the user settings had no Walkthrough section (openspec/changes/simple-tour-and-readable-labels). `nav` is merged over the manifest's own `nav`: the brand block at the top of the navigation (PqDashboard, AppZijbalk) names the app, and the instance's name comes from its theming capabilities through `@theming.name` and its mark through `@theming.emblem|@theming.logo` (the active set's emblem from thematiq, the wordmark when the set ships none), so no municipality is written here; an instance that answers nothing shows the app's name alone. `menu` is merged BEFORE the manifest's own menu; buildManifest merges entries by id and the FIRST definition of a key wins, so an entry here that carries only `id` and `order` keeps its label, icon and route from the manifest, and an entry the manifest does not know (the captions, Contact moments, Appointments, Organisations, Modules and more) is added as written. `pages` holds page overlays. THE PIPELINQ KEYS `modules`, `modulesCaption` and `home` are read by src/utils/menuModules.js.
_meta.removalsNote: The first six are the full profile's own removals, repeated because buildManifest takes ONE list; the spec fails when the two drift. The rest leave the simple menu and stay one step away: `Contacts`, `Tasks` and `OperationalDashboard` have a card on the Modules page, `SlaAttainment` a card on Reports, and `Bookings` is replaced by `AppointmentsMenu`, which opens the same page from the top level. `PointOfSale` and `SettingsIntegrationsCaption` are empty shells in the manifest (a label and no route). The full profile fills the first with children and, since nextcloud-vue 2.84.0, keeps the second as the caption above Connections and BI export in its settings; this flat menu removes both by name. The ids of a module that is switched off are added to this list at boot, by applyMenuModules.
_meta.settingsNote: The first three are the full profile's. `Services` and `Resources` join them: what can be booked and with whom is set-up, the bookings themselves are daily work. `SavedReplies` too: the team writes them once, agents pick them where they answer.
_meta.viewsNote: `ContactMomentsMenu` opens the tickets list narrowed to ticketType `interaction`, and `OrganisationsMenu` the clients list narrowed to type `organization`. Both values are enum members of the seeded schema (register.d/99-unify-ticket-supertype.json, pipelinq_register.json), so they are the same on every instance. A filtered list is a view, not a page. Known gap: CnAppNav decides `active` by route name and ignores `query`, so each pair lights up together.
_meta.modulesNote: A module is a set of menu entries that a municipality does not need and a business does. Every module is OFF in the simple menu until an administrator names it in the setting `menu_modules` (a comma separated list of the keys below). `ids` are the manifest entries that leave the menu while the module is off. `menu` is what joins the profile menu when it is on, under the one caption `modulesCaption` declares. Off or on, every entry has a card on the Modules page (src/manifest.d/98-modules.json), which the footer entry `ModulesMenu` opens. The full profile ignores modules: it shows everything, as before.
_meta.homeNote: The app opens on `/`, and `/` is the Sales overview. In the simple profile the contact centre dashboard is the start page: `/` redirects to `home.page`, and the page that owned `/` moves to `home.rootMovesTo` so it keeps an address of its own. The full profile has no `home` and keeps `/` as it was.

pages._note: The ticket page in the simple structure (openspec/changes/simple-ticket-page). The full structure has no overlay, so its page is today's page. STAGE: `status`, the ticket's own lifecycle field. EVERY STATUS CHANGE HERE IS A TRANSITION OF THE SCHEMA'S x-openregister-lifecycle, posted to OpenRegister's transition endpoint, which checks the `from` state and the authorization again. `visibleWhen` only hides a button on a status its transition cannot leave; it decides nothing. The spec fails when an action names a transition the schema lacks or shows on a status outside the transition's `from`. THE DESIGN NAMES THREE THINGS PIPELINQ DOES NOT HAVE and they are not invented: a reminder to a customer who does not answer (the waiting stage offers Answer again), a step from answered to closed (resolved, completed, rejected, converted and closed are all final, so a finished ticket has no primary button), and a convert-to-case header action (conversion needs an availability answer first, so it stays the self-hiding section it is). A CONTACT MOMENT HAS NO CUSTOMER TO ANSWER: Answer hides on it, the stage then has no primary button, and Close the ticket is in the More menu. THE ANSWER IS WRITTEN IN ONE PLACE: `customer-reply` leaves the body and opens as a dialog from the Answer button, and the body shows the conversation to read. THE GRID IS ONE TABS WIDGET, full width: beside the side column the grid is narrow, and three cards side by side would stack. LOG CONTACT SEEDS THE TICKET AND NOT THE CUSTOMER: the library leaves a token it cannot resolve in place, so `@object.contact` on a ticket without a contact would be saved as those fifteen characters, a foreign key to nothing. `@objectId` always resolves. The contact moment hangs on the ticket, and the ticket names the customer. THE WHAT-NOW CARD (DqZaak, Acties: one next-step button inside a card that lists what the step still needs): `nextStep` names a checklist per stage on fields the ticket has (assignee, client, slaDeadline, portalReplies), and the stage's primary button sits in the card. A finished ticket has no stage entry, so it shows no card. Nothing in the checklist is a guess: an item is done when its field holds a value.

pages._note: The contact centre dashboard in the simple structure (openspec/changes/simple-contact-dashboard). The design's widgets come first and every widget the page had follows, moved down by 15 rows and otherwise untouched: the spec fails when an old widget or an old layout entry differs in anything but `gridY`, or when two cards share a grid cell. EVERY NUMBER IS A FILTER ON REAL FIELDS, and a stat links to the list with the same filter as its query, so the number and the list agree. `Waiting for me` is the same filter as the tickets list view of that name. THE DESIGN SHOWS THINGS A TICKET CANNOT ANSWER and they are left out, not invented: the response time this week (no ticket field holds when the first answer went out), the one named ticket in the attention card (a banner counts, it cannot name a record, so the card says how many are late), the customer's initials and name in the list (a ticket holds its client as a reference without a name) and how long a ticket waits as a duration (the list shows the date it came in, oldest first). `Open` is not one number either: the count endpoint and the list spell a set of statuses differently, so the stats each use one status. THE ATTENTION CARD'S FILTER IS FLAT: `slaDeadline[lt]`, not `slaDeadline: { lt }`. A visibleWhen source is read through the objects list, and the library's query builder writes a nested operator as one JSON value, which OpenRegister answers with a 500 (live check, 5 October 2026). The bar's `occurredAt: { gte }` is nested on purpose: it goes to the aggregation endpoint, whose own flattener reads that shape. DATES IN THE LISTS carry `format: date-time`, or the cell prints the stored ISO text. THE ATTENTION CARD CARRIES `text` AS WELL AS `title`, with the same words: the dashboard gives up the grid cell of any banner whose `text` is empty before it looks at the condition (nextcloud-vue 2.60.0, CnDashboardPage isCollapsedWidget), so a card with only a title and a reason never rendered (live check, 5 October 2026). The attention layout shows the title and does not repeat the text. THE BOARD (PqDashboard, 6 October 2026): the attention card's first action is the primary one; the two lists that are the reader's own work (Waiting for me, Contact today per channel) take two thirds of the row and the two the reader looks up (Callbacks, Latest contact) the right third; the type of a waiting ticket is a pill, drawn by the cell renderer from the column's enum with the same labels the ticket page's type pill uses; and Waiting for me links to the whole list with the filter it counts by. The customer's initials and name and the waiting time as a duration stay out, as above. ROUND 12 (PqDashboard, 16 October 2026): the page header carries the title, the greeting with the date and the Log contact button beside availability, so the greeting and the availability widgets left the grid (availability is the page's own header component), and the client picker beside the title is taken out because the Start a contact card does that job; the four counts carry no icon and a caption with its own count; the three lists draw rows (initials, title, customer and channel, a type pill, how many days it waits, a chevron) instead of tables; the grid closes up behind each card.

pages._note: The tickets list in the simple structure (openspec/changes/simple-contact-dashboard). No view is dropped: the four the page had keep their filter and gain a count, three join them, five show and the rest sit behind the overflow chip. `Waiting for me`, `New` and `Waiting for customer` use the same filters as the dashboard stats that link here. THE AVATAR IS THE HANDLER'S: `assignee` holds a Nextcloud user id. The design draws the customer's initials, and a ticket holds its client as a reference without a name. THE COLOUR IS ON THE DEADLINE: late or due today is red (`lte 0`), due within two days is amber. How long a ticket has waited cannot be coloured, a date rule counts days until a date and a wait lies in the past. BOARD PqTickets: no menu per row (a row opens the ticket, where Edit and the rest live; copy and delete stay on the selection), and the footer says how the list is sorted.

pages._note: The queue in the simple structure, as board PqWachtrij: Download and Take the oldest in the header, three tiles (unassigned, how long the oldest has waited, and within the deadline: the waiting tickets minus those past their deadline, out of all waiting ones, through `limitSource` and `limitStyle: "of"`, nextcloud-vue stat-limit-of-a-count), the type tabs with a channel strip under them, as DqTeamwachtrij draws its lenses (Dq wins over the board's in-card lenses), rows without column heads (`hideTableHeader`), and per row the wait, the title with the customer and channel, the type, the priority, Take on as a pill and View as an eye beside it with no menu (`rowInlineActions`, nextcloud-vue index-row-inline-actions). No search field, no add button and no column filters: a queue is worked from the top. No checkbox: a queue row is picked up, not selected. TAKE THE OLDEST is POST /api/tickets/assign-oldest, which assigns the first open unassigned ticket by occurredAt to the reader. THE LONGEST WAIT is the occurredAt of the first row of the same list, oldest first, read through the list endpoint and drawn as a day count. BESIDE THE LIST: Team today reads GET /api/routing/team-load (every agent profile, its open items and its capacity) and draws a load bar per colleague (record-list `bar`, nextcloud-vue L28); Agreements is a text card with a link to the service levels (text `link` and translated text, nextcloud-vue L27). Until those land the bar and the link are ignored and the text shows untranslated. THE CHANNEL STRIP: channel is a free string and each ticket type stores its own spelling (phone and web on requests and complaints, telefoon and balie on contact moments), so each pill lists its spellings in `values` (nextcloud-vue filter-strip-option-values). Before that library change an option without `value` is skipped and the strip stays away, as it was.
